How to write AI prompts for art?
A well-crafted prompt can help you achieve better results. With Fotor AI image generator, you don’t need prompt engineering skills. Our built-in AI Prompt Enhancer is designed for beginners. Just enter a few simple words, and the AI will automatically expand them into a descriptive, high-fidelity prompt using professional lighting and composition terms.
Tips for writing better AI art prompts:
1. Use synonyms. Use specific synonyms like little, minor, compact, or mini instead of small.
2. Use quantifiers and collective nouns. Specify numbers like “Three dogs” instead of “dogs.” Collective nouns like “herd of zebras” work better than “zebras.”
3. Focus on what you want to see. It is better to describe what you want instead of what you don’t want. If you enter a prompt with “no buildings,” your image will probably appear with buildings.
4. Focus on details. Try to be clear about any details that matter to you. Specify the subject, medium, environment, lighting, color, mood, composition, etc.
5. Specify the lens. Don’t just ask for a “photo.” Indicate the lens type to control perspective and background blur—for example, “85mm lens” for portraits or “14mm wide-angle” for landscapes.
6. Define the light. AI often defaults to flat lighting. Specify the light source and time of day, such as “Golden Hour,” “Volumetric Lighting,” or “Neon Rim Light,” to enhance mood and emotional impact.
7. Describe the material. Focus on surface textures rather than just objects. Use descriptions like “Brushed Metal,” “Distressed Leather,” or “Translucent Silk” for more realistic results.
8. Use double quotes for text. For models supporting typography (e.g., Nano Banana Pro), treat text like a “Quote” and specify font styles like Serif, Bold, or Neon to ensure accurate rendering.
